function.arguments:
{"title": "every 0s is accepted as a reminder interval, so Every.Next divides by zero", "body": "Cause: schedule/every.go parseEvery accepted any duration that duration.Parse returned, including zero. "every 0s" (and "every 0h0m") therefore produced Every{Interval: 0}, and Every.Next (schedule/every.go, the `after.Sub(e.Start) / e.Interval` line) panics with "integer divide by zero" when POST /v1/reminders stores the rule and computes the first due time.

Reports: cr_ae4ae4 (x2, v1.4.0, commit 9c41e7a), POST /v1/reminders with body {"every":"every 0s","text":"ping"}.

Fix: parseEvery now rejects a non-positive interval with "schedule: interval ... must be positive", so the bad rule is refused at input (400) instead of crashing later.

Reproducer: schedule/every_zero_test.go, TestParseRejectsZeroInterval.

Note for follow-up: duration.Parse("") indexes s[len(s)-1] and panics on an empty string. "every " with nothing after it reaches it through schedule.Parse, so that input can still crash. It is not in these reports and was not changed here.", "fingerprint": "fp_096c34", "root_cause": {"file": "schedule/every.go", "function": "parseEvery"}, "reproducer": {"file": "schedule/every_zero_test.go", "function": "TestParseRejectsZeroInterval"}}
